messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "Things feel… unsettled, but not yet breaking. Everyone’s watching, talking a little more, but still careful—like the air’s holding its breath. I’ll keep you posted if anything shifts."
Sender 2: "Just a heads-up — things feel… unsettled. I’ve heard a few quiet warnings lately, and the usual routines are starting to slip. Maybe it’s nothing, but I’m keeping my head down and watching closely. Be careful who you talk to."
Sender 3: "The mood’s shifting — people are talking more, reaching out, testing the air. Be careful what you say, but also pay attention to who’s listening. Things feel unstable, like the ground could shift at any moment."
Sender 4: "The air’s different these days — people are talking, quietly, in ways they wouldn’t have a few months ago. Still no clear direction, but the silence after the meeting last week said more than words ever could."
Sender 5: "The air feels different — quieter, but not relaxed. Something’s shifting beneath the surface, and while they’re still in control, they’re not pretending anymore. I’ve been hearing the same odd clicks on my phone as others. If you’re listening, meet at the old bookstore tomorrow. No names."
Sender 6: "The weather’s been strange lately—sudden heat, then cold snaps. Still, the gardens are holding up, and the markets are full. Just a quiet feeling that things are… holding together, for now."
Sender 7: "The mood’s shifted—people are talking more freely, and even the quiet ones seem uneasy. I’ve heard too many uncoordinated whispers on the same thing to believe it’s just coincidence. Keep your eyes open, but your mouth shut."
Sender 8: "Hey — just wanted to say I’ve been keeping an eye on things, and the quiet shifts are adding up. Nothing’s changed on the surface, but there’s a new kind of stillness in the air — like everyone’s waiting to see who blinks first. Let’s stay sharp, but stay calm."
Sender 9: "Just got back from the market—saw a whole street full of kids playing, no one looking over their shoulder. Feels like everyone’s pretending nothing’s changed. Be careful what you say, even now."
Sender 10: "The air feels tense but quiet — like the calm before a storm that might not come. Just a heads-up: keep your eyes open, but your words light."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
